question: What is the correct way to disconnect an electrical device from the wall socket?

options.A: Switch off the main power breaker
options.B: Grasp the molded plug directly
options.C: Pull firmly on the flexible cord
options.D: Jerk the cable from a distance

explanation: Pulling by the plug prevents internal wire strain and electrical hazards. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: A nurse is moving a heavy oxygen cylinder down the ward corridor. What safety action is required?

options.A: Carry it on the shoulder to save time
options.B: Leave it unsecuring in the middle of the hallway
options.C: Roll it rapidly across rough concrete floors
options.D: Engage safety transport locks and use ramps

explanation: Secure transport prevents heavy cylinders from tipping over and causing severe injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which processing step must always be performed FIRST before disinfection and sterilization?

options.A: Cleaning
options.B: Packaging
options.C: Calibration
options.D: Lubrication

explanation: Cleaning removes organic debris that otherwise protects microorganisms from subsequent germ-killing processes. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which medical device level requires complete sterilization using pressurized steam?

options.A: Plastic basins used for routine bed baths
options.B: Bedside tables touched by visiting relatives
options.C: Surgical forceps entering sterile body tissues
options.D: Rubber tubing used for non-invasive oxygen delivery

explanation: Items entering sterile tissues or the vascular system demand complete destruction of all microbial spores. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: What environmental condition can cause rapid degradation of sensitive hospital electronics?

options.A: Dry and dust-free air
options.B: Adequate ventilation systems
options.C: High humidity and moisture
options.D: Low room temperature levels

explanation: Excessive moisture promotes rust, short circuits, and mold growth on delicate electronic components. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses participate in regular ward equipment stock audits?

options.A: To evaluate the architectural strength of the ward building
options.B: To calculate monthly staff salaries for the hospital accounts department
options.C: To reconcile physical items against inventory records and find missing tools
options.D: To design new medical devices for local manufacturing firms

explanation: Audits ensure all assigned assets are accounted for and ready for clinical deployment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a major vector for spreading nosocomial infections across a hospital ward?

options.A: Storing equipment in dry and clean cabinets
options.B: Proper handwashing before every patient contact
options.C: Using sterile disposable syringes only once
options.D: Improperly decontaminated shared medical equipment

explanation: Shared devices transferred between patients without cleaning carry infectious agents easily. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which practice is NOT effective for decontaminating a blood pressure cuff used between patients?

options.A: Scrubbing away organic soil before disinfection
options.B: Allowing the recommended wet contact time to elapse
options.C: Using an approved chemical disinfectant wipe
options.D: Wiping the cuff surface with a dry cotton cloth

explanation: Dry wiping fails to remove micro-organisms and lacks the chemical action required for true disinfection. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h6)

question: What immediate action must a nurse take upon finding a broken infusion pump?

options.A: Hide it inside a bedside locker until next week
options.B: Leave it plugged in for the next shift to discover
options.C: Tag it out of order and remove it from the active ward
options.D: Attempt to solder the internal circuit board alone

explanation: Immediate tagging and removal prevent accidental clinical use of a compromised device. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why should ward nurses avoid attempting DIY repairs on damaged electrical equipment?

options.A: It saves the hospital too much money on technicians
options.B: It improves the overall warranty coverage of the asset
options.C: It speeds up the return of the device to clinical use
options.D: It creates severe electrocution and fire hazards

explanation: Unauthorized repairs by unqualified personnel increase safety risks and violate hospital policy. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for keeping a patient's bed free of wrinkles?

options.A: To keep the mattress warm
options.B: To make the ward look tidy
options.C: To make linen washing easier
options.D: To prevent pressure ulcer formation

explanation: Wrinkles on bed linen create friction and shearing forces against the skin, which can quickly lead to pressure sores in vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why does a neatly made hospital bed improve a patient's psychological state?

options.A: It eliminates the need for daily medication
options.B: It guarantees a fast discharge from the ward
options.C: It proves that nurses are working hard
options.D: It provides a sense of order and cleanliness

explanation: A clean, well-arranged environment reduces anxiety and promotes a sense of dignity and comfort for hospitalised individuals. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the main danger of shaking used bed linen in the ward?

options.A: It wastes too much nursing time
options.B: It spreads airborne micro-organisms and dust
options.C: It tears the fabric of the sheet
options.D: It makes the linen smell bad

explanation: Shaking linen dislodges settled dust and infectious particles into the surrounding air, increasing the risk of respiratory contamination for others. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h2)

question: Where should a nurse place dirty bed sheets immediately after removing them from a bed?

options.A: On the floor near the bed frame
options.B: Folded neatly on the window sill
options.C: Directly into a laundry hamper
options.D: On the patient's bedside chair

explanation: Placing soiled linen straight into a container prevents the spread of pathogens to the floor, furniture, and surrounding environment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary function of a mackintosh during bed making?

options.A: To keep the patient's feet warm
options.B: To protect the mattress from moisture
options.C: To stop the bottom sheet from sliding
options.D: To decorate the hospital bed

explanation: A mackintosh is a waterproof barrier that prevents urine, sweat, or other fluids from soaking into and ruining the mattress. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is gathering all linen before beginning the procedure important?

options.A: It stops other nurses from taking the sheets
options.B: It prevents leaving a vulnerable patient unattended
options.C: It ensures the linen stays warm in the sun
options.D: It reduces the total weight of the laundry

explanation: Having all supplies ready avoids interruptions that could leave a patient exposed or unsafe while the nurse searches for missing items. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h3)

question: When is an unoccupied bed typically made in the hospital?

options.A: Right after a patient is discharged
options.B: Only during the night shift hours
options.C: When the patient is away or ambulatory
options.D: Before admitting a new client only

explanation: Unoccupied beds are made when the current occupant is out of bed, walking about, or away for tests. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h4)

question: A nurse finishes stripping an empty bed and finds a pair of personal eyeglasses in the sheets. What is the best action?

options.A: Give the glasses to another patient in the ward
options.B: Throw the glasses away with the soiled linen
options.C: Safely store or return the glasses to the patient
options.D: Leave the glasses on the bedside table uncovered

explanation: Checking linen before removal prevents the accidental loss or destruction of a patient's personal valuables. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why does the nurse roll the patient to the side during an occupied bed procedure?

options.A: To check the patient's skin for rashes
options.B: To clear half of the mattress for clean linen placement
options.C: To make the bed look neat from afar
options.D: To help the patient exercise their back muscles

explanation: Rolling the client allows the nurse to change one half of the bed at a time without requiring the patient to stand. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h5)

question: A weak patient on strict bed rest looks frightened when you approach to change their sheets. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask another nurse to hold the patient down firmly
options.B: Explain the procedure step by step before starting
options.C: Skip the bed making until the next visiting shift
options.D: Complete the bed change very quickly in silence

explanation: Explaining actions to a vulnerable client builds trust, reduces fear, and encourages cooperation during physical care. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h5)

question: What safety action must a nurse perform immediately after making a patient's bed?

options.A: Open all the windows in the ward room
options.B: Push the bed close to the nurses station
options.C: Turn off all lights for patient sleep
options.D: Lower the bed and lock the wheels

explanation: Lowering the bed and locking the brakes prevents accidental falls and injuries when the patient gets in or out. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h6)

question: What important clinical observation should be documented alongside the bed making record?

options.A: The time it took to wash the dirty linen
options.B: The color of the mattress padding
options.C: The condition of the patient's skin
options.D: The exact brand name of the bed sheets

explanation: Linen changes offer a vital opportunity to inspect the skin for early signs of pressure damage or breakdown. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary reason for keeping bed linen wrinkle-free?

options.A: To prevent pressure sores
options.B: To improve bed aesthetics
options.C: To keep the ward tidy
options.D: To speed up laundry work

explanation: Wrinkles in bed linen create friction and pressure points that can rapidly damage fragile skin and lead to pressure ulcers in immobile patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why should nurses avoid shaking soiled linen when stripping a hospital bed?

options.A: It prevents the dispersal of dust and micro-organisms into the air
options.B: It stops the linen from tearing into pieces
options.C: It saves time during the morning routine
options.D: It ensures the laundry bags do not get too heavy

explanation: Shaking linen aerosolizes dust, skin flakes, and pathogens, which can contaminate the surrounding environment and spread infection to other patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Where should soiled bed linen be placed immediately after removal?

options.A: Across the back of a wooden chair
options.B: Directly into a designated laundry hamper
options.C: On the floor near the patient's bedside
options.D: On top of the clean bedside locker

explanation: Putting dirty linen straight into a hamper prevents cross-contamination of furniture and keeps the environment clean. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: A nurse is stripping a contaminated bed. What action protects the uniform from pathogens?

options.A: Holding the bundle away from the face
options.B: Folding the linen into tiny squares
options.C: Washing hands before touching the sheets
options.D: Wearing a plastic apron during the procedure

explanation: A waterproof apron acts as a physical barrier preventing microorganisms from the linen from transferring to the nurse's uniform. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: How are the top covers typically arranged on an admission bed?

options.A: Spread flat across the entire mattress surface
options.B: Tucked tightly under the mattress at the top
options.C: Fan-folded to the side or foot of the bed
options.D: Rolled into a tight cylinder at the headboard

explanation: Fan-folding the top linen allows the new patient to slide into bed effortlessly without struggling with tucked-in covers. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: The main purpose of preparing an admission bed is to...

options.A: Keep the room warm for patients with fever
options.B: Support a patient recovering from major surgery
options.C: Isolate an infectious patient from the general ward
options.D: Provide a welcoming and accessible setup for a new arrival

explanation: An admission bed is specially arranged so a newly admitted patient can settle in comfortably and quickly without unnecessary delay. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an operation bed?

options.A: To provide continuous traction for a fractured femur
options.B: To feed a patient who has difficulty swallowing
options.C: To receive a patient recovering from anesthesia safely
options.D: To isolate a patient with a severe airborne infection

explanation: Postoperative beds are specifically structured to ease patient transfer from theater trolleys and manage immediate recovery needs like vomiting or warmth. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why are hot water bottles sometimes placed in an operation bed before the patient arrives?

options.A: To sterilize the surface of the top cotton blanket
options.B: To dry out any moisture left on the mattress cover
options.C: To provide warmth for a patient prone to hypothermia post-surgery
options.D: To weigh down the bottom sheets against movement

explanation: Anesthetics can lower body temperature, so warming the bed helps prevent postoperative hypothermia, though care must be taken to prevent burns. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which patient condition is a cardiac bed primarily designed for?

options.A: Unconscious patients recovering from head trauma
options.B: Heart failure with severe breathing difficulty
options.C: Patients with severe burns over the lower limbs
options.D: Newborn babies with neonatal jaundice

explanation: Cardiac beds support patients who suffer from orthopnea and cannot breathe while lying flat on their backs. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: How does an overbed table help a patient in a cardiac bed?

options.A: It prevents them from trying to get out of bed unaided
options.B: It holds their food tray during regular feeding times
options.C: It lets them lean forward to use accessory breathing muscles
options.D: It supports their intravenous fluid infusion bags securely

explanation: Leaning forward onto a table reduces the work of breathing by engaging the shoulder girdle and accessory muscles of respiration. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the correct ergonomic action for a nurse before making a hospital bed?

options.A: Lower the bed to the lowest possible position
options.B: Adjust the bed height to waist level
options.C: Lock the wheels and step away from the frame
options.D: Remove the mattress to reduce heavy lifting

explanation: Raising the bed to waist height prevents the nurse from hunching over, protecting the lumbar spine from strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why must bed wheels be locked during the bed-making procedure?

options.A: To reduce unwanted noise in the hospital ward
options.B: To make it easier to tuck the bottom sheets tightly
options.C: To prevent the bed from rolling away and causing a fall
options.D: To keep the mattress from shifting out of alignment

explanation: Unlocked beds can shift unexpectedly when a nurse leans against them, creating a major fall hazard for both staff and patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of hospital bed accessories?

options.A: To replace the need for routine nursing physical assessments
options.B: To increase the overall height of the ward bed
options.C: To permanently restrict patient movement in bed
options.D: To enhance patient comfort and prevent bed rest complications

explanation: Bed accessories are primarily designed to support proper alignment and prevent issues like pressure ulcers. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h1)

question: How does a nurse choose which bed accessory to use for a patient?

options.A: According to the personal preference of the ward cleaner
options.B: Depending solely on the manufacturer availability in the store
options.C: Based on individual patient diagnosis and mobility status
options.D: By following a random rotation schedule set by the ward

explanation: Clinical selection of supportive devices always depends on a thorough assessment of the specific patient. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary function of a bed cradle?

options.A: To secure an uncooperative patient safely in bed
options.B: To elevate the patient head for easier breathing
options.C: To prevent the patient from sliding down the mattress
options.D: To lift the weight of bedclothes off the patient

explanation: The rigid frame of a bed cradle creates space over the limbs to prevent pressure from heavy blankets. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient with severe burns on both lower legs requires which bed accessory?

options.A: A footboard
options.B: A bed cradle
options.C: An air ring
options.D: Bed blocks

explanation: Burns are extremely sensitive to friction and weight, making a bed cradle necessary to keep linens off the skin. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why are traditional circular air rings viewed with caution in modern nursing?

options.A: They make it impossible to change patient bed linen
options.B: They are too expensive to purchase for general hospital use
options.C: They cause severe allergic skin reactions in all patients
options.D: They can restrict blood flow to the central tissue area

explanation: The circular design can concentrate pressure around the edges, cutting off capillary blood supply to the middle. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h3)

question: Where is an air ring typically placed under a bedridden patient?

options.A: Underneath the soles of the feet
options.B: Beneath the sacrum or buttocks
options.C: Against the lumbar spine area
options.D: Over the chest and sternum

explanation: Pressure cushions are positioned under bony prominences prone to weight-bearing friction, such as the sacrum. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which bed accessory is specifically used to prevent foot drop?

options.A: Footboard
options.B: Bed cradle
options.C: Backrest
options.D: Air ring

explanation: A footboard provides a firm surface for the soles of the feet, keeping them in dorsiflexion and preventing plantar flexion contractures. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why would a nurse place wooden bed blocks under the foot of a patient's bed?

options.A: To stop the hospital bed wheels from rolling on the floor
options.B: To facilitate postural drainage or specific medical treatments
options.C: To prevent the patient from rolling out of the bed frame
options.D: To make it easier for the nurse to perform bed baths

explanation: Elevating specific ends of the bed frame with blocks helps achieve postural drainage or specific gravity-assisted therapies. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is an essential maintenance step for reusable bed accessories between patients?

options.A: Cleaning with hospital-approved disinfectants
options.B: Submerging the items in boiling water for hours
options.C: Exposing the plastic parts to direct sunlight all day
options.D: Painting the surfaces with bright colored enamel

explanation: Disinfection prevents the transmission of hospital-acquired infections from one patient to another. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is a primary safety check for bed blocks before a patient uses them?

options.A: Ensuring they are stable and secure under the bed legs
options.B: Confirming they are made of soft foam materials
options.C: Making sure they are light enough to kick away easily
options.D: Checking that they match the color of the ward curtains

explanation: Bed blocks alter the structural stability of the bed, so they must be completely secure to prevent tipping or collapse. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary definition of posture in nursing practice?

options.A: The speed at which a patient can ambulate independently
options.B: The amount of pressure exerted on a bony prominence
options.C: The alignment of body parts while holding a position
options.D: The total weight a nurse can lift without mechanical help

explanation: Posture describes how body segments are positioned and aligned relative to each other during static or dynamic states. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is proper body support important for bedridden patients?

options.A: It eliminates the need for routine vital sign checks
options.B: It prevents skin breakdown and joint contractures
options.C: It accelerates the natural healing of bone fractures
options.D: It guarantees complete independence in daily activities

explanation: Proper support distributes body weight evenly and maintains joint mobility, protecting vulnerable tissues from pressure ulcers and shortening. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h1)

question: Where is the center of gravity typically located in the human body?

options.A: In the pelvis
options.B: Within the lower legs
options.C: At the cervical spine
options.D: In the chest cavity

explanation: The human center of gravity sits roughly in the pelvic region, serving as the central point for mass distribution. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: How can a nurse increase physical stability when preparing to lift a heavy object?

options.A: Widen the base of support by spreading the feet
options.B: Stand on one foot to test balance
options.C: Keep the knees completely locked and rigid
options.D: Hold the load far away from the torso

explanation: A wider stance broadens the base of support, helping keep the line of gravity centered and improving overall stability. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does upright posture directly improve respiratory function?

options.A: It increases the total number of red blood cells
options.B: It forces the diaphragm to stop moving during inhalation
options.C: It allows maximum chest expansion for better oxygen exchange
options.D: It decreases the metabolic oxygen demand of lung tissues

explanation: An upright position removes downward pressure from the abdominal organs against the diaphragm, permitting full lung expansion. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which complication is reduced by maintaining proper circulatory flow through good positioning?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Primary hypertension
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Valvular heart disease

explanation: Good positioning and movement prevent blood from pooling in the lower extremities, which minimizes the risk of clot formation. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is a common physiological cause of altered posture in older adults?

options.A: Rapid increase in skeletal muscle mass
options.B: Enhanced neurological reflex speed
options.C: Expansion of intervertebral cartilage discs
options.D: Spinal degeneration and loss of bone density

explanation: Aging often brings degenerative changes to the spine and osteoporosis, leading to structural shifts like kyphosis. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why might a patient with chronic severe pain exhibit a slumped posture?

options.A: To guard painful body areas and limit uncomfortable movement
options.B: To intentionally increase their overall base of support
options.C: To improve blood circulation to the lower extremities
options.D: To maximize their lung capacity during quiet breathing

explanation: Protective guarding is a common behavioral response to pain, often resulting in abnormal muscle tension and poor alignment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: What term describes an exaggerated inward curvature of the lumbar spine?

options.A: Lordosis
options.B: Scoliosis
options.C: Kyphosis
options.D: Footdrop

explanation: Lordosis represents a forward swayback curve typically localized in the lower lumbar vertebrae. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of footdrop in immobile hospitalized patients?

options.A: Prolonged plantar flexion without adequate mechanical support
options.B: Excessive dorsiflexion exercises performed too quickly
options.C: Sudden fractures of the calcaneus bone in the heel
options.D: Inflammation of the subcutaneous tissues in the sole

explanation: Without foot supports, gravity pulls the toes downward, causing the calf muscles and Achilles tendon to shorten into contractures. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h5)

question: What should a nurse look for first when assessing a patient's standing posture?

options.A: The exact blood pressure in both arms
options.B: Symmetry in shoulder and hip heights
options.C: The resting heart rate and respiratory depth
options.D: Skin temperature across the lower back

explanation: Comparing bilateral landmarks like shoulders and hips reveals uneven skeletal alignment and potential spinal curvature. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h6)

question: A patient demonstrates an unsteady, swaying gait during a mobility assessment. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with written instructions
options.B: Restrict the patient to strict bed rest without turning
options.C: Implement appropriate fall precautions and assistive devices
options.D: Instruct the patient to run short distances to build strength

explanation: An unstable gait creates an immediate safety hazard, requiring fall prevention measures to protect the patient from injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is twisting the torso while lifting a heavy object dangerous for the nurse?

options.A: It immediately lowers the nurse's base of support
options.B: It places uneven rotational stress on spinal discs
options.C: It makes the center of gravity move toward the feet
options.D: It reduces the total oxygen supply to working muscles

explanation: Combining rotation with heavy loads strains the intervertebral discs, significantly increasing the risk of herniation and injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h7)

question: A nurse needs to pick up a supply box from the floor. What is the correct physical technique?

options.A: Bend at the knees and hips while keeping the back straight
options.B: Keep the legs straight and bend sharply at the waist
options.C: Lift the box quickly while twisting to the left side
options.D: Hold the box away from the body to see the feet clearly

explanation: Using leg muscles to power the lift protects the lower back from excessive strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which device is specifically used to prevent external rotation of the hips in a supine patient?

options.A: Handroll
options.B: Slide sheet
options.C: Trochanter roll
options.D: Footboard

explanation: Placed alongside the patient's thighs, a trochanter roll stops the hips from rolling outward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of placing a footboard on a bedridden patient's bed?

options.A: To keep feet dorsiflexed and prevent footdrop
options.B: To secure mechanical traction weights safely
options.C: To elevate the lower extremities above heart level
options.D: To prevent the patient from sliding toward the headboard

explanation: A footboard provides a firm surface against the soles, maintaining neutral dorsiflexion and preventing Achilles tendon shortening. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a wide base of support during patient transfers?

options.A: To reduce the patient's anxiety
options.B: To keep the nurse's hands completely free
options.C: To speed up the transfer process
options.D: To increase overall stability and balance

explanation: A wide base of support lowers the center of gravity and prevents the nurse from losing balance during heavy lifts. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why should a nurse avoid twisting the waist while lifting a heavy load?

options.A: It makes communication with the patient difficult
options.B: It places excessive stress on the spinal discs
options.C: It uses up too much physical energy
options.D: It immediately causes the patient to fall backward

explanation: Combining spinal rotation with heavy loads is a primary cause of lower back injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h1)

question: What must a nurse assess first before moving a patient from a bed to a chair?

options.A: The patient's ability to bear weight and follow instructions
options.B: The exact weight of the patient in kilograms
options.C: The brand name of the hospital bed
options.D: The color of the patient's room walls

explanation: Knowing a patient's physical capacity helps you decide if they can help or if you need a mechanical lift. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: A patient does about 60% of the physical work during a transfer. How is this level of help classified?

options.A: Maximum assist
options.B: Complete dependent
options.C: Moderate assist
options.D: Independent

explanation: Moderate assistance is used when the patient performs between 50% and 74% of the physical work needed for the movement. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the first safety check a nurse must do before starting a patient transfer?

options.A: Place a pillow on the wheelchair seat
options.B: Lock the wheels of both the bed and the chair
options.C: Adjust the room lighting to a brighter setting
options.D: Close the room door for privacy

explanation: Unlocked wheels allow furniture to slide apart, which is a common cause of accidental patient falls. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary reason nurses change a bedbound patient's position regularly?

options.D: Wipe gently outward away from the urethral insertion site

explanation: Cleaning away from the insertion site prevents pushing bacteria back up the urethra into the bladder. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h5)

question: What term describes a patient's impaired ability to perform daily hygiene tasks independently?

options.A: Cognitive dissonance
options.B: Activity intolerance
options.C: Sensory deprivation
options.D: Self-care deficit

explanation: A self-care deficit identifies a patient's inability to independently manage routine activities like bathing, dressing, and grooming. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to avoid doing tasks a patient can safely perform themselves?

options.A: To speed up the morning ward routine for staff members
options.B: To prevent learned helplessness and unnecessary dependence
options.C: To comply with strict legal hospital documentation rules
options.D: To reduce the hospital's consumption of soap and water

explanation: Encouraging patients to do what they can preserves their remaining physical strength, morale, and sense of personal dignity. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h6)

question: When must a nurse wear clean gloves during patient hygiene activities?

options.A: Whenever the nurse has dry skin on their hands
options.B: Only when the patient has a diagnosed airborne infection
options.C: During every single interaction with a hospitalized patient
options.D: When contact with body fluids or mucous membranes is likely

explanation: Standard precautions require gloves whenever exposure to blood, bodily fluids, secretions, or non-intact skin is anticipated. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h7)

question: Which action represents a breach of infection control during bed bath procedures?

options.A: Wiping from the cleanest body areas to the dirtiest
options.B: Holding soiled linen close to the nurse's uniform
options.C: Performing hand hygiene before putting on clean gloves
options.D: Placing washbasins on clean over-bed tray tables

explanation: Holding dirty linens against the uniform transfers microorganisms to the nurse's clothing, spreading contamination to other patients. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of person-centered hygiene care in nursing?

options.A: Eliminating the need for family involvement in wards
options.B: Ensuring every bed bath is completed within ten minutes
options.C: Respecting patient preferences and preserving personal dignity
options.D: Following hospital administrative schedules rigidly

explanation: Person-centered care prioritizes the patient's individual habits, modesty, and autonomy during vulnerable hygiene procedures. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h8)

question: How can a nurse best promote independence for a patient with mild upper-extremity weakness?

options.A: Wait until the patient regains full strength before bathing
options.B: Perform the entire bath rapidly so the patient does not get tired
options.C: Encourage the patient to wash their face while the nurse assists with the back
options.D: Insist that family members take over all daily grooming tasks

explanation: Partial assistance allows the patient to maintain control and use their remaining abilities without becoming overly fatigued. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h8)

question: What is the main focus of community-centred health care?

options.A: Eliminating traditional medicine practices from rural settlements
options.B: Shifting health services directly into the living environments of populations
options.C: Focusing exclusively on individual inpatient curative treatments
options.D: Expanding high-tech surgical units within tertiary medical centres

explanation: Community-centred care prioritizes bringing health promotion and disease prevention directly to where people live and work rather than waiting for them to visit distant hospitals. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is empowering local populations essential in community-centred practice?

options.A: It guarantees immediate eradication of all infectious diseases
options.B: It removes all financial responsibilities from the national government
options.C: It enables communities to take charge of their own health determinants
options.D: It completely replaces the need for trained professional nurses

explanation: Empowerment builds local capacity, ensuring sustainable health outcomes through active community participation and ownership. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which international declaration formally defined Primary Health Care principles?

options.A: Ottawa Charter
options.B: Alma-Ata Declaration
options.C: Abuja Declaration
options.D: Nightingale Pledge

explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration of 1978 established the core philosophy and foundational principles of Primary Health Care globally. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: A community health nurse collaborates with the local agriculture extension worker to improve infant nutrition. What primary health care principle is demonstrated?

options.A: Intersectoral collaboration
options.B: Tertiary specialization
options.C: Technological advancement
options.D: Biomedical reductionism

explanation: Working across different sectors like agriculture and health addresses the root social determinants of nutritional status. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: What does comprehensive health care integrate into a single continuum?

options.A: Private insurance and commercial pharmacy operations
options.B: Inpatient quarantine and high-dependency monitoring
options.C: Surgical, pharmaceutical, and radiological specialties only
options.D: Preventive, promotive, curative, and rehabilitative services

explanation: Comprehensive health care covers the full spectrum of human health needs, from preventing illness to restoring function and rehabilitation. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: A nurse treats a child for diarrhea and also inspects the family water source. Why is this comprehensive care?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on expensive laboratory diagnostic testing
options.B: It addresses both immediate illness and the underlying environmental cause
options.C: It fulfills mandatory hospital discharge documentation requirements
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pharmaceutical intervention

explanation: Comprehensive care looks beyond the acute episode of disease to examine and correct environmental and social determinants of health. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is a windshield survey during a community health assessment?

options.A: Observing community life and environmental conditions while moving through the area
options.B: Testing drinking water samples inside a sterile microbiology laboratory
options.C: Reviewing past hospital admission registers from the regional medical records
options.D: Administering written questionnaires to every household head inside a clinic

explanation: A windshield survey is an observational method where the nurse assesses housing, sanitation, and community life firsthand. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why is relying solely on clinic attendance records a flawed community assessment strategy?

options.A: It takes too much time for busy nursing personnel to compile
options.B: It violates patient confidentiality policies under health laws
options.C: It generates too much digital data for manual tally sheets
options.D: It misses vulnerable individuals who never reach formal health facilities

explanation: Clinic records suffer from selection bias because they exclude people facing geographical or financial barriers to care. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: What does cultural competence in community nursing primarily require?

options.A: Replacing all traditional health beliefs with strict biomedical science
options.B: Refusing to communicate with traditional birth attendants
options.C: Respecting local beliefs while addressing harmful health practices
options.D: Adopting local tribal scarring traditions personally

explanation: Cultural competence bridges the gap between professional nursing standards and local beliefs without causing alienation. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why should community nurses engage with traditional birth attendants?

options.A: To hand over complete clinical authority to untrained community members
options.B: To increase out-of-pocket expenses for pregnant village women
options.C: To avoid working inside government-approved primary health centres
options.D: To bridge the gap between local practices and safe institutional delivery

explanation: Engaging traditional birth attendants helps redirect high-risk pregnancies to health facilities and improves overall maternal safety. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is a key indicator of sustainability in a community health program?

options.A: Constant replacement of local health volunteers by visiting researchers
options.B: Local community members taking over management of the health initiative
options.C: Permanent deployment of international medical doctors to village clinics
options.D: Continuous heavy reliance on foreign non-governmental organizations

explanation: Sustainability means a project continues to function effectively using local resources and leadership after external support ends. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: How should a community nurse evaluate the success of an immunization campaign?

options.A: By counting the number of empty vaccine vials left in the clinic store
options.B: By checking if international agencies published the report in a journal
options.C: By measuring vaccine coverage rates alongside community involvement
options.D: By evaluating whether the local government increased taxes for health

explanation: Effective evaluation combines hard statistical coverage data with assessments of ongoing local participation and ownership. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed infections
options.B: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.C: Only individuals showing active fever symptoms
options.D: All patients in healthcare settings

explanation: Universal application protects staff and patients from unrecognized bloodborne and fluid-borne pathogens. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why do nurses use standard precautions for every patient, regardless of their diagnosis?

options.A: Diagnostic tests take too long to process
options.B: Infectious status is often unknown or asymptomatic
options.C: Patients feel insulted if tested selectively
options.D: Hospital policy requires it for billing purposes

explanation: Many carriers of dangerous pathogens show no outward clinical signs upon admission. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: How long should you rub your hands together when using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer?

options.A: Five to ten seconds
options.B: Three to four minutes
options.C: 20 to 30 seconds
options.D: One to two minutes

explanation: Friction must be maintained long enough across all hand surfaces to effectively neutralize transient microbes. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: After caring for a patient with Clostridioides difficile colitis, which hand hygiene method is necessary?

options.A: Washing with soap and water
options.B: Applying antiseptic gel without scrubbing
options.C: Wiping hands with a dry sterile gauze
options.D: Using an alcohol-based hand rub

explanation: Alcohol rubs fail to destroy bacterial spores, requiring physical removal via soap, water, and friction. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: When putting on personal protective equipment (PPE), which item should you put on last?

options.A: Protective goggles
options.B: Face mask
options.C: Gown
options.D: Gloves

explanation: Gloves go on last so their outer surface remains uncontaminated while adjusting other gear. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: When must a nurse use sterile gloves instead of clean, non-sterile gloves?

options.A: During routine bed bath and linen changes
options.B: During surgical or invasive aseptic procedures
options.C: Whenever handling standard oral medications
options.D: Whenever the nurse feels uncomfortable

explanation: Sterile procedures demand the elimination of all transient and resident microbes to protect susceptible body cavities. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: If safety-engineered needles are not available, what is the safe technique for recapping a used needle?

options.A: Two-handed direct push method
options.B: Holding the cap upright with bare fingers
options.C: Bending the needle before disposal
options.D: One-handed scoop method

explanation: The one-handed technique prevents accidental puncture of the hand holding the needle cap. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: Why is it unsafe to reuse a syringe for another patient even if you change the needle?

options.A: Hospital accreditation standards forbid plastic recycling
options.B: The plastic barrel will crack under repeated pressure
options.C: Dosage measurements become inaccurate after one use
options.D: Internal components remain contaminated with blood or fluid

explanation: Backflow into the syringe barrel can introduce patient pathogens into multi-dose vials or subsequent injection lines. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: Where should you cough or sneeze if you do not have a tissue?

options.A: Bare hands for quick washing later
options.B: Directly downward onto the floor
options.C: Upper sleeve or inner elbow
options.D: Into the air away from nearby people

explanation: Coughing into the elbow prevents respiratory droplets from depositing onto hands that touch environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: Which type of transmission is primarily stopped by covering your cough or sneeze?

options.A: Parenteral transmission
options.B: Droplet transmission
options.C: Vehicle-borne transmission
options.D: Vector-borne transmission

explanation: Containing sneezes and coughs stops large respiratory droplets from traveling through the air to nearby hosts. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why must you physically clean medical equipment with soap and water before applying a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Organic soil blocks disinfectants from contacting germs
options.B: Cleaning speeds up the air-drying process
options.C: Soap adds a pleasant fragrance to clinical tools
options.D: Disinfectants cannot dissolve hard plastic surfaces

explanation: Proteins and blood residues shield microorganisms, rendering chemical agents ineffective if not washed away first. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the term for inanimate objects, like bedside tables or stethoscope tubing, that can transfer germs between patients?

options.A: Vectors
options.B: Fomites
options.C: Reservoirs
options.D: Carriers

explanation: Fomites include surfaces and equipment that retain pathogens and transmit them to subsequent users. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: If a nurse accidentally gets a needlestick injury, what is the very first thing they should do?

options.A: Apply an alcohol-based skin antiseptic immediately
options.B: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and water
options.C: Squeeze the puncture site to force blood out
options.D: Fill out the formal hospital incident report form

explanation: Immediate mechanical washing reduces viral load at the wound site before post-exposure prophylaxis assessment. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to report a blood exposure injury immediately?

options.A: Vaccination records must be updated annually
options.B: Insurance compensation is denied after twelve hours
options.C: Timely post-exposure prophylaxis reduces infection risk
options.D: Hospital management requires proof for disciplinary review

explanation: Administering prophylactic medications within hours of high-risk exposure significantly lowers seroconversion rates for HIV and Hepatitis B. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of routine bathing in a hospital setting?

options.A: Administering transdermal medications effectively
options.B: Lowering the patient's core body temperature
options.C: Stimulating rapid muscle hypertrophy
options.D: Removing pathogens and dead skin cells

explanation: Routine bathing physically removes sweat, sebum, and microorganisms, thereby reducing the risk of skin breakdown and infection. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is the bed bath considered a vital nursing assessment tool?

options.A: It replaces the need for vital sign monitoring
options.B: It diagnoses specific systemic infections quickly
options.C: It allows close physical contact for skin inspection
options.D: It measures the exact daily caloric intake

explanation: The close contact required during a bath gives the nurse unobstructed access to inspect the entire skin surface for early lesions or pressure damage. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which therapeutic bath is specifically indicated for postpartum or perineal discomfort?

options.A: Sitz bath
options.B: Ice water immersion
options.C: Paraffin wax bath
options.D: Colloidal oatmeal bath

explanation: A sitz bath specifically targets the perineal and pelvic region with warm water to relieve pain, muscle spasms, and congestion. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h2)

question: A patient with severe eczema and intense itching would benefit most from which additive?

options.A: Absolute alcohol
options.B: Strong antiseptic
options.C: Normal saline
options.D: Colloidal oatmeal

explanation: Colloidal oatmeal has anti-inflammatory properties that soothe irritated skin and relieve severe itching associated with conditions like eczema. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h2)

question: In what direction should a nurse wipe a patient's eyes during a bed bath?

options.A: From the inner canthus outward
options.B: From the outer edge inward
options.C: Strictly from top to bottom
options.D: In a circular scrubbing motion

explanation: Wiping from the inner canthus outward prevents debris and drainage from entering the lacrimal duct and causing infection. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h3)

question: A nurse is performing perineal care for a female patient. Which technique prevents urinary tract infections?

options.A: Wiping from the urinary meatus toward the rectum
options.B: Wiping from the rectum forward toward the labia
options.C: Cleansing the anal area before washing the labia
options.D: Using strong antiseptic soaps on the vulva

explanation: Wiping from front to back prevents fecal bacteria from contaminating the sterile urinary tract. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h3)

question: What type of bath is recommended for a newborn before the umbilical cord stump falls off?

options.A: Whirlpool hydrotherapy
options.B: Medicated tar bath
options.C: Sponge bath
options.D: Full immersion tub bath

explanation: Sponge baths are used for newborns to keep the umbilical cord stump dry and prevent localized infection until it detaches. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why must an infant never be left unattended during a bath?

options.A: Cold water drafts can lower their temperature instantly
options.B: Infants can drown quickly in very shallow water
options.C: They tend to swallow excessive amounts of soapy water
options.D: They will immediately pull out the bathtub plug

explanation: An infant's lack of motor control and top-heavy build places them at immediate risk of drowning in minimal water if left unobserved. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h4)

question: How should a nurse dry the fragile skin of an elderly patient after a bath?

options.A: Patting gently with a soft towel
options.B: Using a high-heat electric hair dryer
options.C: Allowing the skin to air dry completely
options.D: Rubbing vigorously to stimulate blood flow

explanation: Patting the skin prevents friction and mechanical shear forces that can easily tear fragile geriatric skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why is the selection of soap particularly important when bathing elderly patients?

options.A: Elderly skin produces excessive oils that trap harmful bacteria
options.B: Alkaline soaps permanently stain aged epidermal layers
options.C: They are prone to severe allergic reactions to artificial scents
options.D: Their skin has reduced sebaceous gland activity and dries easily

explanation: Aged skin produces less natural oil, so harsh or alkaline soaps strip away the remaining moisture barrier, leading to painful cracking and pruritus. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary definition of oral hygiene in nursing care?

options.A: Practices that keep the mouth and teeth clean and disease-free
options.B: Using strong chemical mouthwashes to sterilize the entire digestive tract
options.C: The surgical removal of decayed teeth and infected gum tissue
options.D: Applying fluoride treatments exclusively during routine dental visits

explanation: Oral hygiene encompasses all habits and nursing interventions that maintain the cleanliness and health of the oral structures. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why does poor oral hygiene pose a risk to the rest of the body?

options.A: It immediately stops the production of digestive enzymes
options.B: It permanently blocks the upper airway
options.C: It directly causes sudden heart valve failure
options.D: Bacteria in the mouth can spread and cause infections elsewhere

explanation: Pathogens multiplying in an unkept mouth can enter the bloodstream or respiratory system, causing widespread infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which tools are essential for checking a patient's mouth?

options.A: Penlight, tongue depressor, and gloves
options.B: An otoscope and a nasal speculum
options.C: Digital thermometer and blood pressure cuff
options.D: Sterile surgical blade and suture kit

explanation: Adequate lighting and a tool to move the tongue are necessary to clearly visualize all oral structures during a nursing assessment. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h2)

question: A nurse inspecting a patient's mouth notices dry, sticky mucous membranes and thick saliva. What does this suggest?

options.A: Normal aging of the gums
options.B: Dehydration or reduced saliva production
options.C: Advanced tooth decay
options.D: An acute bacterial infection of the tonsils

explanation: Dry oral mucosa and thick secretions are classic clinical signs of fluid volume deficit or decreased salivary output. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the medical term for painful inflammation of the mouth lining, often seen after chemotherapy?

options.A: Gingivitis
options.B: Stomatitis
options.C: Dental caries
options.D: Oral candidiasis

explanation: Stomatitis describes generalized inflammation and ulceration of the soft tissues lining the mouth. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h3)

question: How does oral candidiasis (thrush) typically present in a patient's mouth?

options.A: Receding gum lines with exposed roots
options.B: White patches on the oral mucosa that can scrape off
options.C: Loose teeth with pus at the base
options.D: Bright red blisters on the outer lips

explanation: Oral candidiasis typically presents as creamy white patches that leave a red, bleeding surface when wiped away. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h3)

question: What is the main safety risk when providing mouth care to an unconscious patient?

options.A: Aspiration of fluids into the lungs
options.B: Uncontrolled bleeding from the gums
options.C: A sudden drop in blood pressure
options.D: Accidental swallowing of the toothbrush

explanation: Unconscious patients lack protective airway reflexes, making aspiration of rinse water or saliva a major risk during mouth care. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h4)

question: How should an unconscious patient be positioned during mouth care to prevent choking or fluid entry into the lungs?

options.A: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle
options.B: In the Trendelenburg position
options.C: Flat on the back with the neck extended
options.D: Side-lying with the head turned

explanation: A lateral position allows fluids to pool in the side of the mouth and drain out freely, preventing airway entry. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why should regular toothpaste be avoided when cleaning removable dentures?

options.A: It changes the color of the artificial teeth
options.B: It is too abrasive and scratches the denture material
options.C: It neutralizes the denture adhesive
options.D: It reacts chemically to create gas

explanation: Standard toothpastes contain abrasive agents that damage acrylic resin dentures, creating crevices for bacterial growth. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h5)

question: A patient asks why their clean dentures are stored in water overnight instead of being left dry. What is the correct reason?

options.A: To keep the artificial teeth soft for the morning
options.B: To keep family members from misplacing them
options.C: To prevent the denture material from drying out and warping
options.D: To kill remaining bacteria chemically

explanation: Acrylic dentures must remain moist to maintain their shape and fit properly in the patient's mouth. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h5)

question: How long should a person brush their teeth to ensure adequate plaque removal?

options.A: Ten seconds
options.B: Five minutes
options.C: At least two minutes
options.D: Thirty seconds

explanation: Dental health guidelines recommend brushing for a full two minutes to effectively clean all tooth surfaces. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h6)

question: At what angle should toothbrush bristles be placed against the gum line during brushing?

options.A: Flat at a 90-degree angle on top of the tooth
options.B: Facing outward toward the cheek
options.C: Parallel to the tooth surface
options.D: At a 45-degree angle toward the gum line

explanation: A 45-degree angle allows the bristles to slip slightly under the gum margin to sweep away plaque effectively. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary substance that makes up the nail plate?

options.A: Keratin
options.B: Melanin
options.C: Elastin
options.D: Collagen

explanation: Keratin is a tough, fibrous protein that hardens epidermal cells to form protective structures like nails and hair. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which part of the nail structure is responsible for generating new nail growth?

options.A: Cuticle
options.B: Nail matrix
options.C: Lunula
options.D: Nail bed

explanation: The nail matrix contains actively dividing cells that push older cells forward to form the hard nail plate. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary infection control reason for keeping patient fingernails clean and short?

options.A: Preventing pathogen accumulation
options.B: Enhancing dermal drug absorption
options.C: Stopping excessive nail growth
options.D: Improving local blood flow

explanation: Microorganisms easily collect under long nails and transfer to wounds or the face during contact. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h2)

question: A nurse checks a patient's fingernails primarily to gather what type of clinical information?

options.A: Degree of joint inflammation
options.B: Systemic health status clues
options.C: Level of subcutaneous hydration
options.D: Rate of skeletal muscle growth

explanation: Changes in nail color, shape, and texture often reflect underlying conditions like hypoxia or anemia. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h2)

question: What term describes the spoon-shaped, concave nails often linked to iron deficiency anemia?

options.A: Leukonychia
options.B: Koilonychia
options.C: Clubbing
options.D: Cyanosis

explanation: Koilonychia refers to thin, depressed nails with raised edges resembling the shape of a spoon. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h3)

question: A patient with chronic lung disease presents with nail beds showing an angle greater than 180 degrees. What is this called?

options.A: Transverse ridging
options.B: Spoon shaping
options.C: Nail clubbing
options.D: Partial separation

explanation: Clubbing involves gradual thickening and rounding of the fingertips due to long-term oxygen deprivation. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which tool is safest for cleaning debris from underneath the patient's nail bed?

options.A: Hypodermic needle
options.B: Surgical forceps
options.C: Wooden orange stick
options.D: Metal probe

explanation: Wooden orange sticks have a blunt, softer edge that minimizes the risk of puncturing the underlying nail bed. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why should sharp metal instruments be avoided when cleaning beneath a patient's nails?

options.A: They dull the fingernail surface
options.B: They speed up fungal infections
options.C: They can puncture the nail bed
options.D: They dissolve the natural keratin

explanation: The nail bed is vascular and sensitive; sharp tools easily break the skin and cause painful trauma. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the recommended duration for soaking nails before performing routine nail hygiene?

options.A: 30 to 45 minutes
options.B: 10 to 15 minutes
options.C: 1 to 2 minutes
options.D: 1 hour or more

explanation: Soaking for 10 to 15 minutes adequately softens hard keratin plates and loosens accumulated debris. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h5)

question: How should a nurse shape a patient's fingernails during routine hygiene care?

options.A: Round down the corners deeply
options.B: Cut them into sharp points
options.C: Taper the sides heavily
options.D: File straight across

explanation: Filing or cutting straight across prevents the corners from curving inward into the surrounding skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h5)

question: What complication makes routine nail cutting hazardous for patients with advanced diabetes?

options.A: Total absence of natural keratin
options.B: Excessive thickening of the skin matrix
options.C: Peripheral neuropathy and poor circulation
options.D: Rapid overgrowth of the nail plate

explanation: Neuropathy masks pain from accidental cuts, while poor circulation delays healing and invites severe infection. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h6)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with peripheral vascular disease. What is the safest approach to nail maintenance?

options.A: Cutting the corners as deep as possible
options.B: Applying strong chemical removers
options.C: Filing nails gently instead of clipping
options.D: Soaking feet in very hot water daily

explanation: Filing minimizes the risk of accidental lacerations that could easily develop into chronic ulcers in compromised limbs. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h6)

question: What term refers to an infection of the skin fold surrounding the nail plate?

options.A: Onychomycosis
options.B: Koilonychia
options.C: Cyanosis
options.D: Paronychia

explanation: Paronychia is a localized skin infection around the nail margin usually resulting from trauma or bacteria. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is the appropriate initial nursing action for a localized, mild paronychia infection?

options.A: Scraping the nail bed with a blade
options.B: Applying warm saline soaks
options.C: Excising the nail plate immediately
options.D: Bandaging tightly without cleaning

explanation: Warm soaks help relieve inflammation, promote drainage, and reduce discomfort associated with localized nail infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary reason hair care is included in daily nursing tasks?

options.A: To promote patient comfort and hygiene
options.B: To prevent the growth of facial hair
options.C: To speed up the patient discharge process
options.D: To diagnose underlying systemic infections

explanation: Routine hair care directly impacts a hospitalized patient's physical comfort and personal cleanliness. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h1)

question: A bedridden patient refuses to let the nurse comb their matted hair. What should the nurse prioritize first?

options.A: Respecting patient autonomy while explaining hygiene benefits
options.B: Cutting the hair immediately without permission
options.C: Ignoring the hair condition until discharge
options.D: Forcing the procedure to maintain hospital standards

explanation: Nursing care must balance hygiene needs with patient rights and dignity through gentle communication. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which protein makes up the primary structural component of human hair?

options.A: Elastin
options.B: Fibrin
options.C: Keratin
options.D: Collagen

explanation: Keratin is a tough, fibrous protein that forms the main structure of hair, nails, and outer skin layers. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary function of sebum secreted by glands in the scalp?

options.A: Anchoring the hair root firmly
options.B: Providing pigmentation to the shaft
options.C: Lubricating the hair and skin
options.D: Regulating internal body temperature

explanation: Sebaceous glands produce sebum to keep the hair and surrounding skin moisturized and protected. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h2)

question: What technique must a nurse use to properly inspect a patient's scalp?

options.A: Parting the hair systematically in sections
options.B: Palpating without visual inspection
options.C: Shampooing vigorously before looking
options.D: Observing only the hairline from a distance

explanation: Systematically parting the hair allows clear visualization of the underlying scalp skin for lesions or abnormalities. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which factor is the primary mode of transmission for head lice infestations?

options.A: Direct head-to-head contact with an infested person
options.B: Infrequent shampooing and poor personal hygiene
options.C: Sleeping on hospital linen washed in cold water
options.D: Sharing untreated drinking cups with hospital staff

explanation: Head lice spread primarily through direct hair contact, and infestation can happen to anyone regardless of cleanliness. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h3)

question: What part of the hand should the nurse use when massaging a patient's scalp?

options.A: Pads of the fingers
options.B: Palms pressed flat
options.C: Knuckles firmly closed
options.D: Sharp fingernails

explanation: Using the finger pads prevents accidental scratching and trauma to the sensitive scalp tissue. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: A bedridden patient needs a hair wash in bed. What equipment is essential for this procedure?

options.A: Chemical hair removal cream
options.B: Sterile surgical draping sheets
options.C: A high-pressure water hose
options.D: Waterproof shampoo basin or trough

explanation: A waterproof trough directs water away from the bed linens and patient's gown during a bed shampoo. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why does coiled or tightly curled hair require special care during detangling?

options.A: It grows much faster than straight hair types
options.B: It repels all forms of water and liquid products
options.C: It breaks easily when dry due to its structural shape
options.D: It never requires any form of washing or combing

explanation: Coiled hair textures have sharp bends along the hair shaft that create natural weak points prone to breakage. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the best initial action when caring for a patient with unfamiliar cultural hair styling?

options.A: Remove all braids immediately to check for hidden skin lesions
options.B: Ask the patient or family about their preferred hair care routine
options.C: Wash the hair using standard hospital soap without consulting anyone
options.D: Refuse to touch the hair to avoid damaging the existing style

explanation: Consulting the patient or family ensures culturally sensitive care and maintains their personal dignity and preferences. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of a head lice infestation?

options.A: Complete baldness patches
options.B: Patchy hair color loss
options.C: Intense scalp itching
options.D: Excessive hair growth

explanation: Pruritus, or intense itching caused by insect saliva reacting with the skin, is the hallmark symptom of head lice. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard approach for managing mild dandruff?

options.A: Applying harsh chemical relaxers
options.B: Using zinc pyrithione shampoo
options.C: Massaging the scalp gently
options.D: Washing hair on a regular basis

explanation: Harsh chemical relaxers irritate the scalp further and are not used to treat standard dandruff conditions. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: What key detail must be recorded in the patient chart after performing hair care?

options.A: The total number of individual strands of hair lost
options.B: The exact brand of shampoo bought by the hospital
options.C: Patient's exact future hair styling preferences
options.D: Condition of the scalp and interventions performed

explanation: Documentation must reflect the patient's physical findings and the specific hygiene care provided during the shift. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h7)

question: What condition can result from repeatedly pulling hair into very tight braids over a long period?

options.A: Traction alopecia
options.B: Seborrheic dermatitis
options.C: Alopecia areata
options.D: Pediculosis capitis

explanation: Constant tension on the hair roots from tight hairstyles damages follicles and leads to hair loss known as traction alopecia. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h7)

question: What is another common medical name for a pressure sore?

options.A: Venous stasis ulcer
options.B: Decubitus ulcer
options.C: Diabetic foot lesion
options.D: Contact dermatitis

explanation: Pressure sores are frequently referred to as decubitus ulcers due to their tendency to form while lying down. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why do pressure sores develop primarily over bony prominences?

options.A: Tissue is trapped between bone and a hard surface
options.B: Skin is thinner and lacks sweat glands there
options.C: Bone presses outward against external surfaces
options.D: Blood flow is naturally absent in those areas

explanation: External pressure compresses soft tissue against the underlying skeleton, cutting off capillary blood supply. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which body area is most at risk when a patient lies flat on their back?

options.A: Clavicle
options.B: Sacrum
options.C: Ischial tuberosity
options.D: Greater trochanter

explanation: The sacrum bears a large amount of body weight when a patient is in the supine position. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: A patient spending hours in a wheelchair is most likely to develop a sore on the...

options.A: Occipital bone
options.B: Acromion process
options.C: Lateral malleolus
options.D: Ischial tuberosity

explanation: Sitting puts direct weight and pressure squarely on the ischial tuberosities of the pelvis. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h2)

question: What happens during a shearing force injury?

options.A: Sweat softens the skin barrier against the mattress
options.B: Friction removes the top layer of dry epidermal skin cells
options.C: Skin and bone slide in opposite directions, twisting blood vessels
options.D: Direct body weight completely stops all venous blood return

explanation: Shear occurs when skeletal structures move downward while friction holds the outer skin fixed, stretching local blood vessels. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which factor directly lowers the structural resilience of skin against pressure?

options.A: Malnutrition
options.B: High fever
options.C: Tachycardia
options.D: Hypertension

explanation: Inadequate nutrient intake deprives skin and soft tissues of the building blocks needed to maintain strength and repair damage. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: How is a Stage 1 pressure injury best identified on a patient with light skin?

options.A: Open blister with clear fluid
options.B: Non-blanchable erythema
options.C: Black leathery scab formation
options.D: Deep crater exposing muscle

explanation: Stage 1 is marked by redness that does not turn white when you press your finger against the skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why is a pressure sore classified as unstageable?

options.A: Dead tissue covers the base so true depth is hidden
options.B: Infection has destroyed the surrounding anatomical landmarks
options.C: The wound has healed over but left a permanent scar
options.D: It is caused by moisture rather than physical pressure

explanation: Slough or eschar blocks the view of the wound bed, preventing the nurse from determining how deep the damage goes. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which solution is safest for routine cleansing of an open pressure sore?

options.A: Rubbing alcohol
options.B: Undiluted bleach
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide
options.D: Normal saline

explanation: Normal saline is isotonic and cleans the wound without harming newly forming granulation tissue. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of debridement in pressure sore management?

options.A: Drying out excess moisture in deep craters
options.B: Stopping minor bleeding from surface capillaries
options.C: Removing dead tissue to allow healthy healing
options.D: Sealing the wound shut against external bacteria

explanation: Necrotic tissue acts as a barrier to healing and a breeding ground for bacteria, so it must be cleared away. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the standard frequency for turning a bedbound patient to prevent pressure sores?

options.A: Once a day
options.B: Once per shift
options.C: Every two hours
options.D: Every six hours

explanation: Repositioning a patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on vulnerable capillaries. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: How do barrier creams assist in pressure sore prevention?

options.A: They harden the epidermis against sharp shear forces
options.B: They increase local blood circulation in deep muscles
options.C: They shield skin from moisture and chemical irritation
options.D: They replace the need for regular patient repositioning

explanation: Barrier creams create a hydrophobic layer that stops urine and sweat from breaking down the skin barrier. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the medical term for the act of swallowing?

options.A: Mastication
options.B: Deglutition
options.C: Peristalsis
options.D: Regurgitation

explanation: Deglutition is the medical term that describes the entire physiological process of swallowing food and liquids. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h1)

question: What anatomical structure protects the trachea from food entry during swallowing?

options.A: Epiglottis
options.B: Esophageal sphincter
options.C: Uvula
options.D: Soft palate

explanation: The epiglottis folds downward over the larynx and trachea during the pharyngeal phase to prevent food from entering the airway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which laboratory value is commonly reviewed during a basic nutritional assessment?

options.A: Serum albumin
options.B: White blood cell count
options.C: Prothrombin time
options.D: Serum creatinine

explanation: Serum albumin levels provide a useful indicator of protein status and overall nutritional health. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h2)

question: A confused elderly patient refuses meals and shows rapid weight loss. What is the immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Order total parenteral nutrition from the medical doctor
options.B: Insert a nasogastric tube immediately without further evaluation
options.C: Perform a comprehensive nutritional and cognitive screening
options.D: Discharge the patient home with family members

explanation: A structured assessment identifies the root causes of poor intake before invasive interventions are considered. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h2)

question: What is a classic clinical sign that suggests a patient may be aspirating during a meal?

options.A: Complaints of localized joint pain
options.B: Increased abdominal girth
options.C: Sudden skin flushing
options.D: Wet or gurgling voice quality

explanation: A wet, gurgling voice after swallowing indicates that fluid or food particles are resting near the vocal cords. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why do stroke survivors face a high risk of silent aspiration?

options.A: Normal protective laryngeal reflexes are absent without showing outward coughing
options.B: They always refuse food items containing high amounts of sodium
options.C: Esophageal peristalsis speeds up dramatically after a brain injury
options.D: Salivary gland production increases to overwhelming daily volumes

explanation: Neurological damage can impair sensory nerves in the throat, preventing the cough reflex that normally clears the airway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h3)

question: What is the proper bed angle for feeding a bedridden patient safely?

options.A: High Fowler's position at 45 to 90 degrees
options.B: Low semi-Fowler's position at 15 degrees
options.C: Trendelenburg position with tilted pelvis
options.D: Flat supine position with pillow removed

explanation: Sitting upright uses gravity to assist downward movement of the bolus and protect the airway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why is a chin-tuck position recommended during swallowing for at-risk patients?

options.A: It narrows the entrance to the airway to prevent aspiration
options.B: It increases saliva production in the sublingual glands
options.C: It relaxes the abdominal muscles during chewing
options.D: It stretches the esophagus to speed up gastric emptying

explanation: Tucking the chin alters the geometry of the pharynx, directing food safely away from the trachea. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the main reason for alternating solid bites and liquids during a meal?

options.A: To clear food residue left behind in the oral cavity
options.B: To ensure equal distribution of daily water intake
options.C: To dilute stomach acid before digestion begins
options.D: To speed up the total time spent eating the meal

explanation: Alternating liquids and solids helps wash away particles that might otherwise linger and slip into the airway. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h5)

question: A patient with mild hand tremors struggles to hold a standard spoon. What nursing action supports independence?

options.A: Switch the client exclusively to clear liquid supplements
options.B: Provide adaptive weighted utensils and a plate guard
options.C: Feed the patient every meal without offering tools
options.D: Insist that family members visit to assist every meal

explanation: Adaptive equipment compensates for tremors and physical limitations, allowing the client to feed themselves safely. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h5)

question: Which food consistency is most appropriate for a patient with severe dysphagia and no teeth?

options.A: Pureed
options.B: Regular solid
options.C: Mechanically soft
options.D: Regular fibrous

explanation: Pureed foods require zero chewing effort, making them safe for clients with severe swallowing and dental impairments. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h6)
